solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eccentric chap, a Welshman

parts.note: an eccentric is a cam, an off-centre wheel in machinery
Brian is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: Someone describes an odd fellow they met as a Welshman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective for the chap, but it is a noun here: the engineering part.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambria is the Latin name for Wales, so a native of it is a Welsh person.

clue.text: Notice from this source inspiring Queen's devotion

parts.note: an ad is a notice, as in a newspaper

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: hence means from here, from this origin
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An announcement from on high reveals the monarch's devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherence is steady loyalty or attachment to a cause or person, which is devotion.

clue.text: Transport chief performing in the street?

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport
a king is a chief or ruler

explanation.surface: A head of transport is caught entertaining passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Busking is playing music or performing in public places for money; the question mark flags the descriptive definition.

clue.text: Doctor in Iowa, one for feet

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A physician working in Iowa is a specialist in feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a podiatrist; the feet are metrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambs are metrical feet of a short then a long syllable; this is their Latin plural.

clue.text: Be about to drop off teacher going north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word don is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A tutor heading north is getting sleepy.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod, or nod off, is to doze, letting the head drop as sleep comes.

clue.text: Stout Russian teacher originally in old college

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, an old type of British college

indicators.note: originally means the first letters of the words Russian and teacher are taken

explanation.surface: A heavily built Russian taught at a former polytechnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The two initials go inside POLY with no separate signal; 'in' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly describes a rounded, heavy build, which is what stout means of a person.

clue.text: German count's friend's final resting place

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the possessive keeps the S
a grave is where someone is finally laid to rest

explanation.surface: Visiting the burial place of a friend who was a German count.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a count palatine, a German nobleman with royal powers in his region.

clue.text: Linger unhappily at stern of boat in lock

indicators.note: unhappily means the letters of linger are put in a poor, disordered state
the stern is the back of a boat, so the last letter of the word boat is used

explanation.surface: Someone waits miserably at the back of a boat in a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' looks like a canal lock; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Loyal subject, say, tucking into pork pie

indicators.note: tucking into means one piece goes inside the other, while suggesting eating

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie (porky) is a lie
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A faithful follower, for instance, eating a pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is British rhyming slang for a lie; it is not food here.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege, or liegeman, was a vassal bound to serve a feudal lord.

clue.text: So hard entering union circles, ultimately!

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TU is a trade union
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of circles is taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation that hard times finally reached union circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so are synonyms, both meaning therefore or in this way.

clue.text: Disparager's bad name sons endure

parts.note: a name that is mud is a disgraced one
S is the abbreviation for son or sons
to linger is to last or endure

explanation.surface: A critic's reputation is so poor that his sons must put up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flings mud makes malicious attacks on others' reputations, so belittles them.

clue.text: Burrowing rodent in short programme, broadcast internally around India

indicators.note: internally means placed inside the shortened programme word

parts.note: prog is a short form of programme

indicators.note: around means the broadcast word encloses the letter for India

parts.note: aired means broadcast
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A digging animal features in a brief show aired on Indian television.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North American ground squirrel that lives in colonies of tunnels, a burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Dry fellow rising to interrupt

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
Sid is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A man with a dry wit gets up to cut in.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to interrupt them in what they are doing.

clue.text: Stagger back, giving lecherous look

indicators.note: back means the word for stagger is read in reverse

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from an unpleasant, lustful stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive sideways glance.

clue.text: Strike a pose and rise to speak, for example?

definitions.text: Strike a pose and rise to speak, for example?

parts.words: Strike a pose and rise to speak, for example?
parts.note: the clue reads as stage directions, but in word games a pose can rearrange into a peso and rise into sire: rearranged words, of which these are examples

explanation.surface: Instructions for a speaker: adopt a stance, then stand up to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Words formed by rearranging the letters of other words are what the clue's examples show.

clue.text: Lancaster ground inherited from one's forebears

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters of the city name are broken up and remixed

explanation.surface: A Lancaster estate was handed down through the family line.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster is an English city and royal house, which makes the 'ground' sound like land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancestral comes down from earlier generations of a family.

clue.text: Lively grammarian's voice?

definitions.meaning: in grammar a verb's voice is either this or passive

explanation.surface: A grammarian with an animated way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic people are lively, and in grammar the subject-does-it form of a verb has this name.

clue.text: European bishop replaced by very unrefined individual

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: a Bulgarian is a European
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A European churchman is ousted by someone very crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is a coarse, tasteless person, often one flaunting new wealth.

clue.text: Like layer of skin partially under microscope

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something resembling skin tissue is studied under a microscope.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermic means relating to the dermis, the inner layer of the skin.

clue.text: After a month in Paris, man claims right to be hotel manager

parts.note: mai is French for May

indicators.note: claims means the man's name takes in the letter for right

parts.note: Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: After a month in France, a man asserts his right to run the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A maître d'hôtel is the head waiter or manager of a hotel dining room.

clue.text: With misgivings, like one in a French cathedral city

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the city name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
as means like
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone uneasy, like a Frenchman, in a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with misgivings means acting nervously and anxiously, without being at ease.

clue.text: Roll a companion leaves on plate?

parts.note: to spin is to turn or roll
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A bread roll and a companion's leftovers on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb (departs); it is the noun, green leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, so it is leaves served on a plate.

clue.text: Soldier captures leaders of old brigade in desert

indicators.note: captures means the soldier's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letters of old and brigade

explanation.surface: A soldier takes prisoner the commanders of an old brigade in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Japanese port's extremely obvious alias

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of obvious, its first and last

parts.note: aka, also known as, introduces an alias

explanation.surface: A Japanese port has a glaringly obvious other name.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan, on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Vehicle reversed by man wearing gem, not of the highest standard

indicators.note: reversed means the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: wearing means the man's name goes inside the gem, as if dressed in it

parts.note: an opal is a gem
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A vehicle backs into a man in jewellery, a second-rate scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Suboptimal means falling short of the best possible, so below top quality.

clue.text: Cleric cut daughter going to centre

indicators.note: going to centre means the daughter's letter goes into the middle of the word for cut

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: A priest disinherits his daughter, who heads into town.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain or priest, especially in the armed forces.

clue.text: Just cause, providing venue for outdoor entertainment

parts.note: fair means just
grounds are a cause or reason, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A worthy cause provides a site for an open-air show.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is the open site where rides, stalls and shows are set up.

clue.text: Ancient city on eastern river

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An old city stands on a river to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, flowing through Wensleydale.

clue.text: A small number backing WWII alliance

indicators.note: backing means the number word is read backwards

parts.note: six is a small number

explanation.surface: A handful of states lent support to a wartime pact.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany, Italy and Japan formed the alliance opposed to the Allies in World War II.

clue.text: Destructive lout beginning to lurk behind London museum

indicators.note: behind means the letter goes after the museum's letters

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of lurk

explanation.surface: A thug starts lurking behind a London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal wilfully damages property, a destructive hooligan.

clue.text: Representing Nepal, the largest living land animal

indicators.note: representing means the letters stand in for something else, recast in a new order

explanation.surface: Nepal is represented by the biggest beast on land.
explanation.definitionFit: The African bush species is the heaviest land creature alive today.
